baslik: A Satellite Spun Itself to Pieces Weeks After Launch

sahneler.metin: A new Japanese X-ray satellite broke apart weeks after launch.
It spun faster and faster until its solar panels were destroyed.
It began with a glitch in estimating its orientation.
The satellite thought it was rotating when it wasn't.
Its correction added real spin instead.
Then thrusters fired using wrongly set parameters.
That made the spin worse, and the structure failed.
JAXA tightened checks on uploaded commands and settings.
